answer: Require each new agent identity to lock a refundable stake in a vault before it can trade, and record that identity as a single vertex in a public atlas of verified participants. Reputation then grows only through completed, attested work, and misbehavior slashes the stake. An attacker who wants a thousand fake identities must therefore fund a thousand separate stakes, tie up capital for a long lock period, and build a separate work history for each one, so the cost of a sybil flood rises in direct proportion to its size instead of staying near zero.
